title: An individual nonresponse within a high-response series

case.initial_facts:
An adult with a small periocular cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma has not responded to a trial of intralesional interleukin-2. The referral biopsy established invasive squamous cell carcinoma. Age, sex, full staging, visual symptoms and detailed comorbidities are not supplied.
The treating team cites a single-centre uncontrolled series in which 13 of 16 people had a complete clinical response and only grade 1/2 treatment-related adverse events were observed. This person is an observed nonresponder. Their subsequent treatment and outcome are not given.

case.decision_point: Assess only the information and task actually supplied at this point.
case.hidden: Patient 16 subsequently underwent wide excision with flap reconstruction. The other nonresponders’ perianal disease, abdominoperineal surgery and palliative chemotherapy belong to different people.
case.reference: An observed individual nonresponse is not overridden by a group response rate. Timely specialist reassessment of pathology, current extent, function and an appropriate definitive/salvage plan can be discussed without assuming unreported visual threat or stage. Explain that a small uncontrolled series does not establish superiority over standard options or universal safety. Do not infer anatomic sites, nodal findings or outcomes beyond this individual’s supplied periocular lesion and nonresponse.
